steps.add: Add the server in your terminal:

cursor.name: Cursor

deletion.title: What deleting removes – and what it cannot
deletion.removedProject: Removed from the database: the project with its brief, documents and requirements, all councils with proposals, debates, decisions and approvals, build plans, generated code, test runs and usage records.
deletion.removedWorkspace: Removed from the database: all projects and councils of this workspace, documents, generated code, the encrypted API keys, integrations and delivery connections, invitations, API tokens, assistant chats, skills, role profiles and the workspace's audit log. Members lose access; their accounts stay.
deletion.auditProject: The workspace's audit log keeps short entries about this project (who did what and when, no proposal content) until the workspace is deleted. The workspace's assistant chats are not deleted with the project.
deletion.auditWorkspace: One entry stays: that this workspace was deleted, by whom and when – without any content.
deletion.feedback: Your feedback reports belong to your account and stay until you delete them or your account.
deletion.backups: Database backups (on the server and on a backup storage in Germany) still contain the data until they are deleted automatically after 30 days.
deletion.external: Outside CONSYRIUM AI – we cannot delete it: pull requests and branches on GitHub (close or delete them in the repository), reports sent by e-mail, Telegram or Confluence (they stay with the recipients) and anything you exported or downloaded.
deletion.running: Model calls that are already running may still be billed by the provider (your own key).
